title: Adaptive discount guardrails and pricebook reconciliation for enterprise deals
creator: Avery Chen
description: Objective: Define a set of conservative, experiment-backed discount guardrails and a reconciliation process for the canonical pricebook that balances sales velocity with revenue protection and answers requirements surfaced by enterprise security questionnaires (SQs). This ticket scopes the governance policy, the approval ladder (auto-approve thresholds vs. manual RevOps approval), and a pricebook update cadence tied to A/B pricing experiments and legal/SQ constraints.
acceptance_criteria: A published discount guardrail matrix (by customer size, contract term, deployment mode) is added to the pricebook Confluence page
Auto-approve thresholds implemented in the quote tooling for discounts <= X% with pre-flight checks (SLA, data residency, release)
Manual approval flow defined for exceptions with required stakeholders (Sales, RevOps, Legal, Product)
Link from enterprise SQ playbook to the relevant discount/compensation language and required artifacts
Experiment bucket and analysis plan created to validate impact on win-rate and average deal size
decision_log: 2026-02-15: Decided to tie discount tiers to two dimensions: ARR band and deployment sensitivity (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Rationale: higher risk for private/VPC with compliance can justify tighter approval.
2026-02-24: Agreed with RevOps to pilot a time-limited auto-approve threshold of 15% for ARR < $250k with standard terms; above that requires RevOps review.
2026-03-02: Legal added clause requiring Security Questionnaire signoff for discounts > 20% when customer requests on-prem or custom SLA clauses.
2026-03-10: Product proposed experiment stratification: control (current flexible discounting) vs. guardrail (new matrix) across EMEA inbound and US enterprise outbound segments.

tradeoffs: Strict guardrails reduce risk of revenue leakage and audit findings but may slow deal closure and frustrate top-performing reps.
Auto-approve improves velocity but increases the chance of inconsistent contract language unless paired with SQ and template checks.
Running experiments delays enterprise-wide rollout but provides quantifiable evidence to support guardrail thresholds.
risks: Sales pushback leading to shadow discounting if the approval flow is perceived as onerous
Incomplete SQ automation causing manual bottlenecks in RevOps
Misalignment between pricebook updates and the quote-tooling implementation window causing temporary mismatches
experiment_plan: Metric(s): win-rate, time-to-sign, average ARR, discount depth, revenue retention at 6 months
Population: segmented by ARR band (<$250k, $250k-$1M, >$1M) and deployment (hosted, dedicated, private)
Duration: 8 weeks pilot with weekly checkpoints
Analysis: p95 confidence intervals with Bayesian uplift modeling; RevOps to own telemetry dashboard
